verdict.rationale: Cognee documents agent-invocable memory operations: `remember` for adding (including into a per-session cache mid-conversation), `recall` for searching, and `forget` for deleting items or datasets. It also ships an official MCP server that MCP-compatible assistants can call, so an agent can drive its own memory through tools or API calls. However, there is no documented operation for editing or updating a specific memory (`improve` only enriches the graph), and the evidence does not list which operations the MCP server exposes as tools. missing for 10: explicit update/edit-memory operation, documented MCP tool list covering add/search/update/delete, independent hands-on corroboration of agent self-managed memory.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my agent can manage its own memory mid-conversation — adding, searching, updating, and deleting memories through tools or API calls it invokes itself

citations.quote: It stores information in memory with a single API call.
cognee.remember(data, session_id="my_session") — writes content directly into the session cache for fast retrieval.
The `.recall` operation is the main retrieval entry point in Cognee v1.0. It searches memory using the best available source for the request.
Single data item deletion: remove one data item from a dataset.
Cognee MCP brings persistent AI memory to your workflow through the Model Context Protocol.
You access them through MCP-compatible AI assistants like Cursor, Claude Desktop, Continue, Cline, and Codex.
